tagline: Cron jobs without the crontab syntax.
description:
Cron Manager lists the current user's cron jobs and lets you add, edit, enable, disable and delete them from a form. Common schedules — at reboot, every minute, hourly, daily at a time, weekly, monthly, yearly — are picked from a list, and the five crontab fields are there when you need something they do not cover.

Run now executes a job immediately and shows you its output and exit code, which is usually how you find out that the path was wrong. Running as root additionally shows the read-only system jobs in /etc/cron.d/.

The second tab is the mvmOS scheduler itself: the single cron entry that drives every installed app's own scheduled work. You can see whether it is installed, which apps are registered with it, and turn it on or off.
capabilities: List, add, edit, enable, disable and delete the current user's cron jobs.
Preset schedules, or the five raw crontab fields.
Run a job immediately and see its output and exit code.
Read-only view of /etc/cron.d/ system jobs when running as root.
Install or remove the mvmOS scheduler cron entry.
See which installed apps have registered scheduled work, and warn when a scheduler file is missing.
